title: E-Beam Inspection - Contamination Detection on Surfscan SP5
subtitle: Post-Anneal Quality Validation for 3nm Node Manufacturing
author: James Rodriguez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Surfscan SP5 system to detect and classify Contamination defects during post-anneal inspection at the 3nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Contamination defects that are critical to yield at the 3nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Surfscan SP5 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Surfscan SP5
- Inspection Type: E-Beam Inspection
- Target Defect: Contamination
- Process Step: Post-Anneal
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 3nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all Surfscan SP5 systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for post-anneal monitoring in the 3nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Surfscan SP5
Software Version: v9.8.981
Recipe: E-BEAM_INSPECTION_3nm_POST_ANNEAL
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (125 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Surfscan SP5 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'E-Beam Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Contamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 3nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 44 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 93% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.5% for E-Beam Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-05-04
Wafers Tested: 45
Total Defects Found: 492
Defect Density: 156.61 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.1%
Capture Rate: 92.0%
Test Duration: 202 minutes
System Uptime: 98.6%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Surfscan SP5 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Contamination at the 3nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
